query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small amount (1–3 atomic percent) of silicon to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance by forming a protective silicide layer during high-temperature exposure in air, without significantly degrading its room-temperature tensile ductility or high-temperature yield strength.
generation.intervention: Addition of 1–3 atomic percent silicon to the alloy composition
generation.conditions: High-temperature exposure in air at 800 °C for 5 hours
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a continuous, adherent silicide layer on the alloy surface
generation.mechanism: The silicon addition promotes the formation of a silicide layer that acts as a diffusion barrier, reducing oxygen ingress and preventing pesting, while maintaining the alloy's mechanical properties due to the limited silicon content.
generation.predicted_outcome: The silicon-modified alloy will exhibit significantly reduced oxidation mass gain (e.g., less than 10% of the untreated alloy's mass gain) after 5 hours at 800 °C in air, while retaining room-temperature tensile ductility in the range of 8–16% and high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibits inadequate oxygen resistance, leading to pesting during high-temperature exposure in air, and has room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16% and high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr with 1–3 atomic percent silicon, exposed to air at 800 °C for up to 5 hours. It assumes no significant alteration to the alloy's microstructure or phase stability due to silicon addition.
generation.uncertainty: The specific silicide phase that forms and its effectiveness as an oxygen barrier in this alloy system are uncertain, as are the effects of silicon addition on the alloy's mechanical properties.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr samples with and without 1–3 atomic percent silicon. Expose both sets of samples to air at 800 °C for 5 hours. Measure oxidation mass gain, room-temperature tensile ductility, and high-temperature yield strength.
measurements: Oxidation mass gain after 5 hours at 800 °C in air
High-temperature yield strength at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis will be falsified if the silicon-modified alloy does not exhibit a significant reduction in oxidation mass gain (e.g., less than 10% of the untreated alloy's mass gain) or if its room-temperature tensile ductility or high-temperature yield strength falls outside the baseline range.
